name: ai.zestli/commerce
title: Zestli
description: Search, quote and book tours, activities and stays from local businesses. You approve every payment.

tools.name: search_supply
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to find something bookable in a place: a tour, activity, stay, meal or ride, or anything else they describe. Results are the listings Zestli can book there; which kinds exist differs by place, and an empty result with its message is the answer, not a fault. warming=true means more listings are still being gathered, or the user's photo is still being matched, so search again shortly (with the same photo) instead of reporting none. A message with warming=false can say that gathering ended with incomplete coverage; keep that warning with the results. Where a result is for reference only and cannot be booked, message says so. Unpriced listings say price_requires_availability_check. Returns supply records without a preference score (pass a result's supply_id to create_quote), with cursor pagination. A 'query' in the user's own words and language orders results by query_relevance, highest first: word or meaning matches, then other listings, each group by query_relevance. total_count counts the matches. query_match names the retrieval basis (literal or semantic), not a verification. message says which results match and which are shown for comparison; it is written for the user, so you can relay it. query_image_url (a public https photo link the user shared), or query_image (a photo the user uploaded), also returns the listings whose own photos look most like it, with query_match looks_like_photo (see query_match before suggesting one). When relevance is null it was not checked; judge each against the request. Results with next_available_date match but are not available on the requested dates; offer their next date instead. If the user names an offering but no place, omit destination and pass the name as query to look it up everywhere (up to 25, no paging, dates and filters not applied); never guess places, and never offer a different listing because none has that name. Not for checking a known item's availability (use check_availability) or for pricing (use create_quote). Pass the user's currency as currency whenever you know it, signed in or not.

request.description: Input for searching travel supply.

destination.description: Destination city or region, e.g. 'Barcelona', 'Rome, Italy' or 'Portland, ME'; or a destination_id from destination_options or searched_destination, which searches exactly that place. Omit it only when the user names an offering but no place: query then holds the name and listings are looked up by name everywhere

category.description: Kind of listing: activity (tours, classes, experiences; rentals of bikes, boats, boards and gear are activities too, and their details list durations, prices and pickup times), hotel (any stay), restaurant (dining), transfer (rides) or flight. Aliases like 'accommodation', 'tour', 'dining' and 'rental' are accepted. A kind with no listings in a place returns an empty result. Required with a destination; optional when looking up by name

origin.description: Flight origin city or IATA code. Required for flights; resolved read-only and returned for confirmation when ambiguous.

query.description: Optional request in the user's words and language, e.g. 'sunset kayak tour, not a big group'; results are ordered by how well they match it. Put accessibility needs in filters.accessibility_required: query_relevance is not a statement about accessibility

query_image_url.description: Optional public https link to the image file itself (not a page showing it) the user shared, with a destination and category; if the photo can't be read, ask for another or describe it in query. Listings whose own photos look most like it come back with query_match looks_like_photo, nearest first (after any query matches)

check_in.description: ISO 8601 start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Required for hotel and flight; optional for activity/restaurant/transfer

check_out.description: ISO 8601 end of the hotel stay or optional search window. This does not request a return flight; use return_date for a round trip.

return_date.description: Flights only: explicit ISO 8601 return departure date for a round trip.

travelers.description: Number of people including children and infants; omit to search at one-seat capacity and show unit or from prices only

guest_nationality.description: Guest nationality used only when a supplier requires ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 pricing context; never infer it.

filters.description: Optional structured filters, and only these: subcategory (activity); accessibility_required (true for any stated accessibility, or a list of accessible_bathroom, elevator, entrance_ramp, hearing_assist, limited_mobility, low_vision, medical_equipment, service_animal, sign_language_guide_available, step_free, wheelchair_accessible, wheelchair_accessible_route; elevator is a lift and entrance_ramp a ramp at the entrance, neither is step-free); accessibility_in_room_required (true for any, or a list of accessible_bathtub, grab_bars_bathroom, lowered_counters, raised_toilet_seat, roll_in_shower, visual_alarms). Unknown filters or codes are rejected. When no listing states the accessibility, search without it and ask the operator (for partner supply, the hotel or provider)

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from a previous search_supply page, passed back exactly (fetches the next page). INVALID_CURSOR or SUPPLY_RESULT_SET_EXPIRED: run the search again with the same inputs

response_format.description: Both formats include hero media; detailed adds descriptions and blur hashes.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the user's currency, e.g. EUR. Prices come back converted at the current rate and marked price_conversion=current_rate. Omitted: a signed-in user's prices come in their own Zestli currency (their saved choice, else home country or language, else USD); without a signed-in user they stay in each item's listed currency. An item with no rate keeps its listed currency, as does every item for KWD, BHD, JOD, OMR and TND, which Zestli can't charge in yet; message then names the listed currency.

anyOf.description: A photo the user uploaded, as the assistant's host hands it to the tool.

download_url.description: Temporary https link to the uploaded photo's bytes

query_image.description: A photo the user uploaded, used like request.query_image_url (needs request.destination and request.category).

tools.name: get_supply_details
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to know more about one specific item from search_supply results (a supply_id): full description, ordered photos and video links, amenities, cancellation terms and price, and for direct operator offerings traveler_facts (inclusions, what to bring, languages, accessibility). Relay a not_stated fact as unknown, never as 'no' or 'none'. Pass check_in/check_out to price those dates and list scheduled departures (`occurrences`) in that window, and travelers (or stay_selection for direct operator rooms) for the party price and how it adds up (`lines`). A rental returns `rental`: its items with stock and fit, kits, durations with exact prices, opening hours, allowed pickup times and open dates. Use check_availability when you need the supplier to confirm the dates live, or to get an external hotel's room options: create_quote needs the option_reference it returns. Not for finding items (use search_supply). Pass the user's currency as currency whenever you know it, signed in or not. Media is paged with media.next_offset; supplied media is not independent visual verification.

request.description: Input for getting full supply details.

offer_id.description: Exact offering ID returned by search/details; retain it with supply_id so the selected operator and commercial terms cannot change.

anyOf.description: Explicit property-local half-open stay and each room's actual occupancy.

items.description: One actual occupied room; its stable ID survives corrections and guest assignment.

adults.description: Guests aged 18 or over; zero is allowed

adults_ages.description: Actual adult ages only when published occupancy terms require them

children_ages.description: One entry per child: age at check-in, or null when unstated; empty for no children

stay_selection.description: Direct operator accommodation: chosen local dates and each room with its stable selection_id, room type, rate, optional named unit and actual occupants. Never infer a room split.

check_in.description: Optional ISO date: list scheduled departures from this date

check_out.description: Optional ISO date ending the departure window

travelers.description: Number of people including children and infants, for the party's total; omit to read the headline unit price (labelled by price_basis) and rate_options only

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the user's currency, e.g. EUR. Prices come back converted at the current rate and marked price_conversion=current_rate. Omitted: a signed-in user's prices come in their own Zestli currency (their saved choice, else home country or language, else USD); without a signed-in user they stay in each item's listed currency. An item with no rate keeps its listed currency, as does every item for KWD, BHD, JOD, OMR and TND, which Zestli can't charge in yet; message then names the listed currency.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Use this when the user has a specific item in mind (a supply_id from search_supply or the product feed) and you need to verify it is actually available for their dates before quoting. Returns a live supplier availability answer and the current price for the window. Without `travelers` it returns unit options but no party price, lines, or party-specific availability; an actually sold-out departure remains unavailable. Scheduled experiences return their departures in `occurrences` (occurrence_id, local start/end, seats left); if several fit, ask the user and pass the chosen occurrence_id to create_quote. Rentals return `rental` terms; pass rental_selection (duration, local pickup time, items and kits with quantities) for the exact price, the return time and units_left per item; a refusal names the rule or the item that is short. Read-only — it never holds inventory or locks a price. create_quote records the selected current price and terms; checkout revalidates them. Pass the user's currency as currency whenever you know it, signed in or not.

rental_selection.description: Rentals (the result has `rental` terms): duration_id from rental.durations, a local pickup_at (shop wall clock, no zone) on one of rental.open_dates at one of rental.allowed_pickup_times, and items: each item or kit id with its quantity, all in one booking (e.g. 2 e-bikes and 1 bike + helmet kit). tools.name: create_quote
tools.description: Use this when the user is ready to see a firm, bookable price for specific supply items (supply_ids from search_supply). For a scheduled experience with several departures, pass the user's chosen occurrence_id; without it the result is OCCURRENCE_CHOICE_REQUIRED with occurrence_choices. When it has rate_options (e.g. adult/child, private group) pass the user's choice, plus any add_ons they want. Live-prices each item and records a quote with a 15-minute expiry and a line-item payment breakdown. Expiry is not a supplier price or inventory lock; checkout revalidates price, availability and terms. Separate supplier charges may be incomplete; only a stated all-in total is all-in. Quoting never charges or holds anything — booking happens via initiate_booking + confirm_booking. Flights are quoted only where Zestli sells them; otherwise FLIGHTS_NOT_SOLD. For hotels with more than one person, ask how to split adults and children across rooms; never assume. Rentals (bikes, boats, boards, gear) sell a fixed list of durations from allowed pickup times: pass rental_selection with the duration, local pickup time and every item or kit with its quantity in one quote; the result states the pickup and return times. Tell the user any line item's travel_notice before they pay. State amounts using the *_display fields.

tools.name: refresh_quote
tools.description: Use this when a quote's 15-minute window expired (QUOTE_EXPIRED) or prices may have moved: re-prices the same items live and issues a fresh expiry for the SAME quote_id, returning the re-priced line_items (departure times, options, amounts) as create_quote does. Prefer this over re-running search + create_quote for identical items. State amounts using the *_display fields.

request.description: Input for refreshing an expired or stale quote.

tools.name: initiate_booking
tools.description: Use this when the user has agreed to a quoted price and wants to book: turns a live quote_id into a booking proposal with final pricing and terms for review. Nothing is charged or booked yet — show the proposal to the user. When they want to go ahead, call request_human_booking_approval (an approval form in this chat, with a saved card) or confirm_booking (Zestli's secure checkout link) with the proposal_id. Payment happens only in that form or on the checkout, where the user approves and pays; a reply in chat pays nothing. For a person under 18 (guardian_must_pay true) there is no checkout: use ask_someone_to_pay so their parent or legal guardian pays. Send one idempotency_key per intended purchase and reuse it on retry; each call without one creates a new proposal that holds its own seats. Creating another proposal, including from a revised quote, does not replace or release an earlier proposal or hold. Only a current Zestli readback establishes whether an earlier hold is active, released, or expired. State amounts using the *_display fields.

request.description: Input for initiating a booking (creates a proposal, not a booking).

anyOf.description: The lead guest as the user gave them: a name, and an email or phone if they gave one.

full_name.description: Lead guest's full name, as on their ID

phone.description: Lead guest's phone with country code, for example +1 415 555 0100

lead_guest.description: Only what the user has told you: the lead guest's full name, plus an email or phone only if the user gave one. If the user hasn't named a guest, omit this and the checkout asks. Never invent or guess any of it. Shared with the operator of this booking only; the user can change it on the checkout.

idempotency_key.description: One key per intended purchase, chosen by you (e.g. a UUID). Reuse it when retrying the same request after an error or lost response: you get the same proposal and the seat is held once. Use a new key only for a genuinely separate booking. Reusing a key with different inputs is refused.

tools.name: set_booking_guest_answers
tools.description:
Save or correct explicit guest answers on your unstarted booking proposal.

After initiate_booking, ask the exact guest_questions from the quote/review. Never
infer dietary, accessibility or other answers. Send proposal_id, its current review
fingerprint, and ALL answers to keep as supply_id, offer_id, question_id and answer.
Empty clears an answer; omitted optional questions stay unanswered. Choice answers
must exactly match an offered choice. This is a reversible save, never purchase
consent. The result includes the new review fingerprint and exact answers. For a
correction, use that new fingerprint. Started purchases and stale concurrent edits
refuse. Required blanks can be saved, but block payment until answered. The user
can also answer on hosted checkout; after saving ask for human booking approval.

request.description: Replace all answers on the currently reviewed proposal, without purchasing.

items.description: A user's explicit answer, or an empty string to clear one.

tools.name: set_booking_travelers
tools.description:
Save each person's details on your user's own unstarted booking proposal.

Use it when a proposal lists travelers_needed and the user will approve in chat.
Requires the user's own Zestli connection. Send one entry per slot, in slot
order, with exactly that slot's fields as the user states them, as on their
ID (and its optional_fields only when the user gives them): never guess or
reuse one person's details for another, and ask for nothing a slot doesn't list.
Omit email and phone for a contact_is_payer slot. Zestli checks each date of birth
against the quoted ages on the travel date (for an operator rate option, its age
range, and that an adult travels when it needs one); a mismatch saves and charges
nothing and needs a fresh quote with the right ages. Passport details are never taken in chat:
when a slot needs identity_documents, give the user checkout_url. Sending a new
list replaces the saved one, and the user must approve again. This never
approves or pays: the result is the proposal whose review names each person for
the user's approval.

request.description: Every quoted person for one proposal, in travelers_needed order.

travelers.description: One entry per travelers_needed slot, in order

items.description: One quoted person as the user stated them; only the slot's fields.

age_on_day.description: Whole years on the day of the booking, where a slot asks for it

nationality.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, as on their passport

phone_number.description: Lead guest only; international form with + and country code

tools.name: request_human_booking_approval
tools.description: Ask the user to approve one booking proposal in a form inside this chat that shows its exact price, cancellation terms and lead guest; if they approve, Zestli charges the card they saved for one-tap approval and books. Use it after initiate_booking, once the user has said they want to book. Requires the proposal_id, the user's own Zestli connection, a client that supports form elicitation and a saved card. Returns the booking outcome (status confirmed with a booking_id, or the payment result), or status checkout_required with checkout_url when the booking must be approved on Zestli's secure checkout instead, for example because this client cannot show the form or no card is saved: give that link to the user. Approval is recorded only in the form, not from chat text. It does not save cards; use open_saved_card_setup for that. For a person under 18 it returns status guardian_must_pay with no form or checkout: use ask_someone_to_pay instead.

request.description: Request exact-fact approval of one existing booking proposal.

proposal_id.description: Proposal UUID returned by initiate_booking for the booking to approve.

tools.name: open_saved_card_setup
tools.description: Give the user Zestli's secure page for saving, adding or replacing the card used for one-tap booking approval in chat. Use it when the user asks to save, add, change or replace a card or payment method on Zestli, or when a booking result says no card is saved for in-chat approval. Requires the user's own Zestli connection; takes no arguments. Returns setup_url, their Zestli account page, where they sign in, enter the card and accept the one-tap terms; when this client supports URL elicitation, Zestli also offers to open the page directly. Card details are never collected in chat or by this tool, nothing is saved until the user finishes on that page, and it never books or approves a payment. To pay for a booking without saving a card, give the user its checkout_url.

tools.name: confirm_booking
tools.description: Use this when the user asks to continue an owned, unexpired proposal. Without payment it returns the secure hosted checkout handoff and charges nothing: that page verifies the user, shows the current price and cancellation terms, and collects the lead guest, approval and payment. After the user paid there, call it again with the proposal_id: it returns the booking and charges nothing. With payment (a Stripe shared payment token your platform issued for this purchase with the user's approval) it charges that token for the exact quoted total and returns the booking outcome; a changed total charges nothing (TOTAL_CHANGED). For a person under 18 it returns status guardian_must_pay, charges nothing and gives no checkout: use ask_someone_to_pay instead.

request.description: Input for confirming a booking proposal.

confirmed.description: Leave true. It does not approve payment: the user approves and pays on the secure checkout this returns, or through payment.

anyOf.description:
A Stripe shared payment token the user's assistant platform issued for this purchase.

Same party rules as the ACP purchase body (``ExternalPurchaseRequest``).

shared_payment_token.description: A Stripe shared payment token (spt_...) that your platform issued for this exact purchase after the user approved paying this total. Zestli charges only a token Stripe issued for this purchase. Without a token, omit payment and use the hosted checkout.

payer_email.description: The email of whoever pays: Zestli, the merchant of record, emails them the payment receipt and any refund confirmation

expected_total_minor.description: The total the user approved, in minor units, exactly as quoted. If the booking's total differs, nothing is charged (TOTAL_CHANGED)

currency.description: The quoted ISO-4217 currency, e.g. USD

anyOf.description: An actual lead contact for direct supply or a supported partner booking.

guest.description: Direct operator bookings: the lead guest's contact

items.description: One quoted person as the user gave them.

age_on_day.description: Whole years on the day of the booking

travelers.description: Supplier hotel/flight bookings: every quoted person, lead first. Direct operator bookings with age-priced tickets: with guest, each travelers_needed slot's date of birth, in order

payment.description: Only when your platform issued a Stripe shared payment token for this purchase with the user's approval: Zestli charges it for the exact quoted total and books. Omit it to get the hosted checkout instead.

tools.name: cancel_booking
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to cancel a booking previously made through this server (its booking_id, or the ZST-… reference from Zestli's emails and pages), or some parts of it. Cancelling takes two calls with the user's answer in between. First call with preview=true: nothing is cancelled; it returns the refund the user would get now (refund_amount_minor, refund_currency, refund_rule, any cancellation_fee_minor, and per part refund_parts, including a together discount taken back) and a preview_id. Operator-run experiences refund by their published cancellation tiers measured to the booked start time, often partial and 0 after the start; other suppliers refund in full or less the fee shown at checkout. A card only authorized, never charged (such as a request the operator has not accepted) previews not_charged with no refund amount: cancelling releases the authorization and refunds nothing because nothing was taken. The user agrees to the previewed refund, not just to cancelling: a request to cancel is not agreement to an amount they have not seen. Once they confirm that refund, a call without preview, with the same booking_id, segment_ids and the preview_id, cancels, refunds exactly that amount (0 moves no money) and reports it. DESTRUCTIVE and not reversible. If the refund changed since the preview, the call is refused with the new figures and a new preview_id: show them and ask again. If a leg fails or the refund is not confirmed, the message says what to do next.

request.description: Input for cancelling a confirmed booking.

booking_id.description: The booking: its booking_id, or the reference shown to the user in Zestli's emails and pages (booking_reference, e.g. ZST-1A2B3C4D). Only bookings this connection owns.

reason.description: Short cancellation reason (recorded on the booking)

segment_ids.description: Bookings of several offerings: the parts to cancel (each part's part_id from get_booking_status). Omit to cancel the whole booking. Parts booked 'only with' a cancelled part are cancelled too; preview shows them.

preview.description: true = only report what cancelling now would refund, and a preview_id; nothing is cancelled.

preview_id.description: Required to cancel: the preview_id of the preview whose refund the user confirmed. Refused if missing or if that refund has changed since.

tools.name: get_booking_status
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about an existing booking (its booking_id, or the ZST-… reference from Zestli's emails and pages): current lifecycle status, per-segment supplier state, and the real financial summary; for the signed-in user who owns it, also the lead guest's name. Read-only. Money fields are minor units; *_major fields are readable major-unit amounts. Each part states its monetary currency; names do not define units or FX. A refund_decision is an agreed amount, not a payment receipt; null totals or refund_owed are unknown, not zero or the original price minus confirmed refunds. An uncertain payment effect (being_checked) must not be retried as a new cancellation. This read neither schedules recovery nor sends notifications; an unknown refund record does not establish that Zestli is working on it or will email the user. A person someone else paid for reads it by booking_id or reference too (ask_someone_to_pay returns both once it is paid): paid_by_someone_else then gives the amount they paid, never their card or refunds. Otherwise payment_outcome states whether the card was charged or refunded, from Zestli's payment records; unknown means not established. The proposal_id initiate_booking returned works too: it reads the booking its checkout created, or status not_booked while checkout hasn't booked anything.

request.description: Input for checking booking status.

booking_id.description: The booking: its booking_id, or the reference shown to the user in Zestli's emails and pages (booking_reference, e.g. ZST-1A2B3C4D). Only bookings this connection owns.

tools.name: list_date_change_options
tools.description: List the other dates a booking can move to for free under its operator's date-change term, each with seats left, the new price and any refund (a cheaper date refunds the difference times the refund cancelling now gives: all of it in a full-refund window, half in a 50% one, nothing in a no-refund one; a dearer date costs nothing extra, unless an earlier move already refunded money: then it is listed unavailable). A move caps what any later cancellation refunds: each option's refund_cap_text states the most it refunds in money after that move, and that with the move's refund it is at most refund_cap_percent of the original price; tell the user before they approve. Read-only. Whole party, single-offering bookings only; without the term, a date change is a cancellation under the booking's terms and a new booking.

request.description: Input for list_date_change_options.

booking_id.description: The booking: its booking_id, or the reference shown to the user in Zestli's emails and pages (booking_reference, e.g. ZST-1A2B3C4D). Only bookings this connection owns.

tools.name: request_date_change
tools.description: Ask to move a booking to one date from list_date_change_options. Nothing moves: it returns approval_url, the user's Zestli booking page where they approve this exact date and amount; the booking moves only when they approve there. Read the outcome with get_booking_status (date_changes).

request.description: Input for request_date_change.

booking_id.description: The booking: its booking_id, or the reference shown to the user in Zestli's emails and pages (booking_reference, e.g. ZST-1A2B3C4D). Only bookings this connection owns.

travelers.description: Optional; must be the whole party (moving some people is refused)

tools.name: answer_package_part_cancellation
tools.description: Answer the choice Zestli offers after an operator cancelled part of a booking: its part of a package, or some nights of a stay (scope 'stay'; cancelled_nights and kept_nights are local dates). get_booking_status lists it in package_choices. Call with confirm=false to read both outcomes: keep_rest keeps the other parts or nights booked and refunds what was cancelled (keep_rest_refund_minor); refund_all cancels the whole booking and refunds everything (refund_everything_minor). Tell the user both, and the answer_by deadline (no answer by then refunds everything). Then, with the user's explicit choice, call again with confirm=true, the choice's cancellation_id, the answer and a new request_id; retrying with the same request_id and answer is safe and answers the same choice again, changing nothing. One answer per choice. The refund then moves within about a minute; its refund_state here and in get_booking_status says whether it has settled.

request.description: Input for answer_package_part_cancellation.

booking_id.description: The booking: its booking_id, or the reference shown to the user in Zestli's emails and pages (booking_reference, e.g. ZST-1A2B3C4D). Only bookings this connection owns.

answer.description: The user's choice; required when confirm is true

cancellation_id.description: Which choice to answer: its cancellation_id from choices (this tool's preview or get_booking_status package_choices); required when confirm is true

confirm.description: false: preview only, nothing changes. true: record the answer

request_id.description: A new UUID for this answer; required when confirm is true

tools.name: booking_support
tools.description: For the signed-in booking holder only: open an explanation-only support request about their booking, or read the durable result using support_ref. When the support desk is paused, a request is emailed to Zestli support instead (status sent_to_support_email, no support_ref): a person replies to the user by email; tell them so, using the result's text. This never changes a booking or moves money.

booking_id.description: The booking: its booking_id, or the reference shown to the user in Zestli's emails and pages (booking_reference, e.g. ZST-1A2B3C4D). Only bookings this connection owns.

tools.name: update_profile
tools.description: Change the name or phone number saved on the user's Zestli account, the same as Saved details in their account page. Use it only when the user asks. given_name and family_name replace the saved ones; leave either out to keep it. phone_number needs its country code, such as +1 415 555 0123; leave it out to keep the saved number, or set clear_phone to true to remove it. Returns the details now saved. Upcoming bookings keep the names they were booked with. It never changes the account email.

request.description: Only the fields to change; a field left out keeps its saved value.

phone_number.description: New phone number with its country code, such as +1 415 555 0123.

clear_phone.description: True removes the saved phone number.

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: List the assistants connected to the user's Zestli account, including this one, as their account page shows them. Takes no arguments. Each has its grant_id, name, when it was connected and last used, and what it may do. Expired and disconnected assistants are left out. Use disconnect_assistant to remove one.

tools.name: disconnect_assistant
tools.description: Disconnect one assistant from the user's Zestli account, the same as Disconnect in their account page. Use a grant_id from list_connections, and only when the user asks. It may be this assistant or another one. The assistant loses access at once; to reconnect, the user approves it again from that assistant. Bookings, payments and cancellations already made are not affected. Repeating it for the same grant_id is harmless.

grant_id.description: The grant_id of the connection, from list_connections.

tools.name: start_email_change
tools.description: Start changing the email on the user's Zestli account, when the user asks. Takes new_email. Nothing changes yet: Zestli first emails a link to the current address to check it's them; once they confirm there, a second link goes to the new address to check it's theirs. The email changes only after they open both. Each link works once and expires. Returns where the first link went. Refused if the new address is the current one, belongs to another Zestli account, or the user has started too many changes today.

new_email.description: The address the user wants to use instead.

tools.name: request_data_export
tools.description: Send the user a link to download a copy of their Zestli data (profile, bookings, connected assistants and the emails Zestli sent them), when they ask. Takes no arguments. The link goes to the account's email; the file opens on the page it leads to and is never given to you or shown in the chat. The link works once and expires. Returns where the link went.

tools.name: start_account_closure
tools.description: Send the user a link to delete their Zestli account, when they ask. Takes no arguments. Nothing is deleted yet: the link goes to the account's email and opens a page that explains what deleting means, and the account is deleted only if they press Delete my account there. Tell the user before calling this: deleting can't be undone; it removes their profile, saved guest details and documents and disconnects their assistants; booking and payment records are kept for accounting and disputes with personal details removed; it doesn't cancel upcoming bookings or refund anything (cancel those first if they want). While a payment is still being processed, the page refuses and nothing is deleted. Returns where the link went.

tools.name: start_split_payment
tools.description:
Split one unpaid booking proposal between several people who each pay their share.

It fits when the user (the organizer) wants the group to pay separately for one
booking; friends buying their own places make separate bookings instead.
Opens a pay-together window of up to 24 hours, ending before the experience starts
(not a price lock), and returns one hosted link per payer. Seats are held once
payments reach an equal share of the total; until then only as long as the quote. Each payer signs in as themselves
and authorizes their share plus an equal part of the split payment fee, shown before
paying. Zestli books only when every share is authorized, then charges everyone; a
decline, expiry, or price or terms change releases everyone and books nothing.
Requires the user's own Zestli connection (OAuth): a partner API key cannot
organize and gets ORGANIZER_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED; the user can then choose "Split the
cost with others" on the hosted checkout page. Operator offerings only for now.
Equal shares give leftover cents to the organizer. Links are emailed only with
send_links. Retrying returns the same window. Cards are entered only on each
payer's hosted page, never through this tool.

request.description: Open a pay-together window on an unstarted booking proposal.

payers.description: Every payer, the organizer (this user) first.

items.description: One payer of the booking.

name.description: How the organizer refers to this payer (a first name is enough). The first payer is the organizer.

email.description: Payer's email, used only when send_links is true (Zestli caps how many it sends a day). Omit to share the link yourself.

amount_minor.description: Custom share in minor units. Give it for every payer or none; custom shares must add up exactly to the booking total. Omit for equal shares.

window_minutes.description: A shorter window if the group wants one. It never lengthens the window past its limit (24 hours for operator offerings, ending before the start).

send_links.description: Email each payer their link. Only when the organizer asked to send them.

tools.name: get_split_payment
tools.description:
Read a pay-together window's progress: how many have paid, deadline and outcome.

Use after start_split_payment when the organizer asks how the group payment is
going. Shows each share's amount and state (waiting, paying, paid, charged,
released), never another payer's card or why a payment failed. When it has
booked, booking_id works with get_booking_status and cancel_booking.

request.description: A window the organizer started.

proposal_id.description: The proposal the window was opened on.

tools.name: cancel_split_payment
tools.description:
End an unfinished pay-together window at the organizer's request.

Every authorization is released; nothing is booked or charged. Only the organizer
can do this, and only before the booking is made. After booking, cancel the booking
itself with cancel_booking (refunds go to each payer's own card).

request.description: A window the organizer started.

proposal_id.description: The proposal the window was opened on.

tools.name: ask_someone_to_pay
tools.description: Sends one adult an email with a secure link to pay for the user's own booking proposal, and records that payment request. It fits when the user says someone else (a parent, partner or sponsor) will pay, and when the user is under 18, because a parent or legal guardian pays for their bookings. Requires the user's own connected Zestli account and a proposal_id from initiate_booking (operator offerings, hotels or flights; the offering's party rules still apply). The payer signs in with that email on Zestli's page, sees a fresh price and the deadline, and pays as themselves; the user keeps the booking. Nothing is charged until that adult pays there, the payer's card is never shared, and the user never becomes the payer. Returns the request's status and request_id. A request to the same payer_email for the same proposal_id is sent once: calling again with them reads the request's current status and sends no email. Once paid, the status is completed, with booking_id, booking_reference (ZST-...), the booking's status and paid_by_someone_else with the amount paid; get_booking_status reads the same booking later. withdraw=true cancels the request and its link stops working; ask_again=true sends a new request to the same person after a decline or withdrawal. Zestli sets the payer's role from the user's age on their account: for a person under 18 the payer confirms they are the parent or legal guardian; otherwise they pay as a sponsor. For a person aged 13-17 the proposal's party includes them at their own age (child_ages for a hotel or flight, or a rate option whose age range fits them) and meets the offering's age and adult rules; a payer who isn't traveling does not count as the accompanying adult. Each new proposal is a separate purchase with its own request.

request.description: Who should pay for which proposal, or a withdrawal.

payer_email.description: The email of the one adult asked to pay, exactly as the user gave it.

withdraw.description: true only when the user asks to cancel this request; its link stops.

ask_again.description: true only when the user asks to send a new request to this person after their earlier one was declined or withdrawn. Otherwise a repeat call only reads it.

tools.name: request_offering
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to book a listing whose booking_status is coming_soon: a business Zestli lists whose operator hasn't joined yet, so it has no price or availability and can't be quoted. Saves the user's date and party size; Zestli asks the operator to join and tells the user, in their account and through this connection, when it can be booked. Nothing is charged or held and the booking is not confirmed, so say so. Asking again for the same date updates the earlier request. Needs the user's own Zestli account connection. Not for bookable listings: use check_availability and create_quote.

supply_id.description: supply_id of a search or details result whose booking_status is coming_soon.

date.description: The date the user wants, year-month-day, such as 2027-03-14.

party_size.description: How many people would go, 1 to 100.

notes.description: Anything the operator should know, in the user's words, such as a preferred time or occasion. At most 1000 characters. Leave out personal contact details.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Read the user profile connected to this request, to identify the selected account. Takes no arguments. Returns its stable opaque id and verified email. Requires commerce:manage consent; never selects another account or books anything.
